title: Durable project instruction contract
description: Objective: establish concise durable project instructions for every provider without copying generated assignments or live Moe state into source control. Deliverables: canonical root AGENTS.md, a minimal root CLAUDE.md bridge, one focused instruction-contract checker/test, and a short ownership note if needed. AGENTS.md owns tool-neutral architecture boundaries, verification commands, explicit-path staging, shared-tree ownership, fail-closed truth, and source-size rails. CLAUDE.md contains only Claude-specific bootstrap/runtime guidance and points to AGENTS.md rather than duplicating it. NOT in scope: task-specific prompts, session transcripts, worker IDs, provider credentials, live .moe state, or generated .codex instructions. Hard dependencies: none. Owned paths: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and a new isolated checker/test path selected by the architect; avoid modifying active package sources.
definitionOfDone: Root AGENTS.md is concise, canonical, tool-neutral, and contains no live task, worker, branch, or session state.
Root CLAUDE.md is a thin Claude bridge to AGENTS.md with no duplicated normative policy and no secrets or generated assignment content.
A deterministic checker fails on missing bridge/canonical markers, oversized files, or forbidden generated/live-state markers without rewriting either file.
Fresh focused verification and repository regression checks exit 0; only explicit owned paths are staged and committed.
taskRails: Keep durable project policy separate from generated provider/session instructions.
Do not edit or delete live .moe, .codex, .claude/settings.local.json, role, skill, task, message, channel, or agent state.
Keep each instruction file short; link to deeper docs rather than accumulating a large prompt.
Use TDD for the checker and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, merge, reset, or stash.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — author the instruction-contract checker test FIRST at tests/instruction-contract/checker.test.ts (root vitest.config.ts already includes tests/**/*.test.ts, so NO config or package-source edits are needed or allowed). Test a pure function checkInstructionContract(input: { agents: string | null, claude: string | null }): Violation[] where Violation = { code, file, detail } and code is one of the stable reason codes: AGENTS_MISSING, CLAUDE_MISSING, CANONICAL_MARKER_MISSING, BRIDGE_MARKER_MISSING, BRIDGE_REFERENCE_MISSING, FILE_OVERSIZED, GENERATED_MARKER_PRESENT, LIVE_STATE_MARKER_PRESENT. Synthetic-fixture cases (mutation-resistant, assert exact code + file): (1) null content -> *_MISSING; (2) AGENTS content without literal marker '<!-- instruction-contract: canonical -->' -> CANONICAL_MARKER_MISSING; (3) CLAUDE content without '<!-- instruction-contract: bridge -->' -> BRIDGE_MARKER_MISSING; (4) CLAUDE content that never mentions 'AGENTS.md' -> BRIDGE_REFERENCE_MISSING; (5) oversize: AGENTS > 120 lines or > 8192 bytes, CLAUDE > 40 lines or > 2048 bytes -> FILE_OVERSIZED (count lines via split(/\r?\n/) and bytes via Buffer.byteLength for CRLF/Windows safety); (6) content containing 'moe-generated' -> GENERATED_MARKER_PRESENT; (7) live-state ids: /\b(task|epic|chan)-[0-9a-f]{32}\b/, /\b(worker|architect|qa|governor)-[0-9a-f]{8}\b/, or literal 'Approval mode:' -> LIVE_STATE_MARKER_PRESENT; (8) fully valid pair -> exactly []. IMPORTANT: a plain mention of the '.moe/' directory in policy prose is ALLOWED — do not ban it; only the id/marker patterns above are forbidden. Also add two integration tests that read real root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from disk (resolve repo root from the test file location, not process.cwd()) and assert zero violations. Run `pnpm exec vitest run tests/instruction-contract` and confirm it FAILS (checker module and md files don't exist yet) — that red run is this step's evidence.
implementationPlan.note: Added the RED contract suite first, covering every stable reason code, both line/byte caps, all live-ID families, generated markers, allowed .moe prose, empty content, deep freezing, exported caps/patterns, deterministic valid input, and two repo-root integration cases. Fresh RED command `pnpm exec vitest run tests/instruction-contract` exited 1 exactly because `./checker.js` is absent, as planned.

implementationPlan.description: Implement tests/instruction-contract/checker.ts to make the synthetic-fixture tests green. Pure core: checkInstructionContract takes file CONTENTS (string | null), returns frozen Violation[] — no fs, no process access, no writes ever (checker is read-only by contract; it must never rewrite or autofix the md files). Thin loader helper loadInstructionFiles(rootDir) that reads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md with utf8 and maps ENOENT (or any read error) to null — fail closed: unreadable means MISSING violation, never a pass. Export the size caps and forbidden-pattern list as named frozen constants so the test asserts against the same values. Keep the file <=250 lines, no dependencies beyond node:fs/node:path. Synthetic tests green after this step; the two real-file integration tests still red (md files absent) — expected.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented a 174-line dependency-free, read-only checker with frozen caps/patterns/results, stable violations, CRLF-safe line counts, UTF-8 byte caps, exact durable/live marker checks, and a fail-closed loader mapping all read errors to null. Focused run: 22 synthetic tests pass; only the two planned real-file integration tests fail with AGENTS_MISSING/CLAUDE_MISSING because the root files are not authored yet.

implementationPlan.description: Author root AGENTS.md — canonical, tool-neutral, <=120 lines and <=8192 bytes. Must contain the literal marker '<!-- instruction-contract: canonical -->' near the top. Sections: (1) Purpose — canonical durable project instructions; provider files bridge here. (2) Architecture map — pnpm workspace: packages/contracts (shared types/codecs, no deps), packages/scheduler, packages/store, packages/control-room-model, packages/testkit, apps/daemon (bounded ingress consuming contracts+scheduler); dependency direction flows toward contracts; adapters/* reserved. (3) Verification — `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (root vitest covers packages/** and tests/**), `pnpm verify:foundation`, `pnpm verify:store`; note apps/daemon tests run only via `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (root gate does not discover apps/**). (4) Git discipline — stage explicit owned paths only; never `git add -A`/`git add .`, push, merge, reset, or stash; no sibling worktrees. (5) Shared-tree ownership — multiple agents work concurrently in this one tree; touch only paths your task owns; preserve foreign work; never edit live .moe/, .codex/, or .claude/settings.local.json state (this section IS the required ownership note — no separate file). (6) Fail-closed truth — stable reason codes; missing/unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority; advisory envelopes stay frozen and advisoryOnly. (7) Source-size rails — target <=250 lines per production source, split before 400; TDD for every behavior change; no debug/scratch/generated-evidence files in commits. (8) Pointers — authoritative design doc D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-design.md (read-only, never edit), CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/plans/. HARD exclusions (checker enforces): no task/epic/channel/worker ids, no 'moe-generated' marker, no 'Approval mode:' line, no session/branch state, no secrets. Link deeper docs instead of inlining detail.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review + explicit-path commit. (b) does the checker treat empty-string content as present-but-marker-missing (violations) rather than crashing or passing? (c) CRLF vs LF: do line/byte caps behave identically on Windows checkout (.gitattributes normalization) — split on /\r?\n/, bytes via Buffer.byteLength? (d) does the checker ever write? grep the checker for writeFile/appendFile/unlink — must be none; (e) are all reason codes reachable and asserted at least once? (f) no scratch/probe files anywhere under repo root (wrapper auto-commit sweeps the entire dirty tree — delete strays BEFORE the terminal moe call). planningNotes.risks: (1) Self-referential trap: while writing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md prose it is easy to embed a forbidden marker (a task id, 'Approval mode:', 'moe-generated') — the integration tests catch this; describe forbidden things generically in prose. (2) Over-broad forbidden patterns: banning the literal '.moe' string would make legitimate policy prose ('never edit .moe/ state') impossible — ban only id-shaped regexes and generated markers, never the directory name. (3) CRLF: Windows checkout may deliver CRLF; count lines with /\r?\n/ and bytes with Buffer.byteLength or caps drift across platforms. (4) Wrapper auto-commit sweeps the whole dirty tree into a branded commit (see mem:gotcha-moe-wrapper-autocommit) — leave zero stray files before the terminal moe call; worker cannot prevent the sweep itself, do not fight it. (5) process.cwd() differs between root and package-scoped vitest runs — resolve repo root from import.meta / test-file location, not cwd.
